blockers.description: confirmBooking double-charges on a plain double-submit of 'Confirm & pay'. PayMongo does NOT honor Idempotency-Key on POST /v1/checkout_sessions — every POST mints a new independently payable session. Proven by probe: two byte-identical POSTs with the same key returned cs_ed60840548c9ccadc27ba6c3 and cs_6c4e54d253178994b94934b8. A real UAT booker was charged twice: pay_YFn1jgMWyau46ECydfPR2LdN (10:00:35Z) and pay_iw2zsj3ehcRzgRYzgn7hkoUP (10:08:29Z), ₱735.00 each on booking aff63acb-b6a5-45f7-8b47-6a01d589f765 — ₱1,470 collected against a ₱735 booking, unrefundable because both are qrph (src/lib/paymongo.ts:257).
blockers.scope: NOT a CR-02 regression and WIDER than CR-02. No re-price occurred (both charges ₱735 at declared_pax 3, so both calls built the same key checkout:<holdId>:73500). CR-02's expire gate lives in updateDeclaredPax and only fires on a re-price; confirmBooking expires nothing before creating. Flat-priced bookings are equally exposed — their checkout:<bookingId> key was BELIEVED to be a double-charge guard and is not one. This predates Phase 8.

unlogged_findings.description: `included` ('Base price covers') and `max_occupancy` are independent with NO enforced relationship, and declaredPax is clamped to max_occupancy BEFORE the surcharge is computed (src/lib/availability/units.ts:455). So any listing where included >= max_occupancy has a MATHEMATICALLY UNREACHABLE surcharge: extraHeads = max(0, pax − included) is always 0, the host collects nothing extra forever, and nothing warns them.
unlogged_findings.why_it_matters: This is the shape a host is MOST likely to configure, because it is the intuitive reading of the feature. Operator's own example: a pickleball court rated for 8 where the surcharge should apply above 8 — setting included=8, max_occupancy=8 silently yields zero surcharge. For it to fire, max_occupancy must be STRICTLY GREATER than included (e.g. holds 12, base covers 8, heads 9–12 surcharged). The two fields also sit in different steps of the wizard with no cross-reference.
unlogged_findings.suggested_close: Cross-field validation (included < maxOccupancy) plus a line of copy in the Group pricing block. Cheap, but it is a revenue-loss path, not polish.

context_notes: The through-line of this session is one lesson worth carrying into the gaps plan: a mock that echoes back your assumption cannot falsify it. Four plans of test coverage all agreed the Idempotency-Key collapsed duplicate checkout sessions, because the mock was written from the same belief as the code. The only thing that found it was a human clicking a button twice, and then a 20-line probe against the live API. Any fix for this defect that is verified only against the mock has not been verified. Also note the two UAT-environment lessons: a tunnel started inside a subagent dies when that agent exits (which stalled UAT steps 5–8 and looked exactly like a product bug), and PayMongo RETRIES failed webhook deliveries automatically — restarting the tunnel replayed both missed events within a minute with no manual intervention. Both are now in the paymongo-local-webhook-uat memory.
